_____________________________________________________________________________________

Your Capabilities

Want to build the go-to-market engine for a fast growing payments business?

Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for a Payments GTM Operations and Strategy Lead to be part of our Fintech department.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers .

We’re building the financial backbone for field service businesses. Our Fintech team is one of the most strategically important and fastest growing parts of Jobber. We help businesses get paid, access capital, understand their financial health, and ultimately stay in business longer.

The future of financial services is embedded, and we’re still early. Small businesses increasingly rely on vertical SaaS platforms like Jobber not just to run their operations, but to manage their money. This role will own how Jobber’s payments business grows. Think of this as running the commercial side of a payments business inside a SaaS company.

jobs.description:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.

We are hiring an Engineering Manager for Ceph & Distributed Storage. The world creates more than 2.5 quintillion bytes of data every day! We want to help teams to store data in open source storage on commodity hardware - safely, cheaply and simply.

Our goal is to make Ceph easy to install, manage and use - from large enterprise data center installations to half-rack edge sites. We believe that distributed storage shouldn’t be hard - and to keep up with the increasing data storage demands, it needs to be easier than ever before. We have a range of tools to bring to bear on the problem, and we're excited to make distributed Ceph easy enough that everyone does it.

As an engineering manager at Canonical you must be technically strong, but your responsibility is to run an effective team and develop the colleagues you manage. You are expected to help them grow as engineers, do important work, do it outstandingly well, find professional and personal satisfaction, and work well with colleagues and community. Technical leadership experience and a background in software engineering are necessary prerequisites for this role. You will be expected to lead, challenge, and develop strong engineers, positively influence the culture, facilitate technical delivery, and work with your team on strategy and execution. You will be responsible for sound software architecture and best practices in software quality, testing and documentation.

What you’ll do

• You will lead a team building a Ceph focused software defined storage solution

• You will build and manage a globally distributed team of engineers

• You’ll develop your team through coaching, mentoring and feedback

• You will demonstrate sound engineering principles by directly contributing toward your team’s goals

• Set reasonable schedules based on considered estimates, with feedback loops for improvement

• Set and manage expectations with other engineering teams and external stakeholders

• Advance modern, agile software development practices

• Maintain a culture of quality and engineering excellence

• Grow a healthy, collaborative engineering culture in line with the company values

• Be an active part of the leadership team and collaborate with other leaders in the organisation

• Work from home with global travel up to 20% for internal and external events

Who you are

• You have a software engineering background, preferably with Python and C++ experience

• You have experience operating scale out storage clusters on Linux in production environments, preferably with Ceph

• You love embracing new technologies and pushing the boundaries of what is possibleYou love developing and growing people and have a track record of doing it

• You have an interest in building products that improve how people operate software and infrastructure everywhere

• You are knowledgeable and passionate about software development

• You have experience in leading, managing, coaching and mentoring software developers towards delivering timely, high quality software together

• You have solid experience working in an agile development environment

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

Bitwarden is looking for a server and cloud enthusiast, with experience in both communicating about and deploying these technologies. You will become a Bitwarden product expert and handle business inquiries regarding our products, troubleshooting technical issues, completing systems integrations, and ensuring customer satisfaction.

This is an all-remote team and we’re looking for someone located in the APAC region.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Functioning as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for Bitwarden and the entire product portfolio

• Leading proof-of-concept trials with customers, new deployments, and/or integrations of Bitwarden containerized services

• Advising customers on industry best practices for the full stack of Bitwarden

• Working with enterprise customers to solve issues and/or look ahead to identify solutions to situations they may face in the future

• Providing superb guidance and assistance for each business prospect or customer’s implementation of Bitwarden, integration with the rest of their technology stack, and general security

• Collaborating with Sales, Engineering, and Product associates

• Assist in planning, developing, and presenting live technical product demonstrations showcasing best practices scaled to the customer’s use-case

• Document and share customer feedback from collaborative sessions to help the Bitwarden team exceed expectations

WHAT YOU BRING TO BITWARDEN

• Excellent English and grammar

• Excellent problem-solving skills (you might not know all the answers but you know how to find and communicate the solutions)

• Project planning, including collaborative and individual time management

• A passion for supporting your team members, growing together (technical ability and emotional intelligence), and sharing your knowledge with all

• A strong sense of empathy and the ability to advocate for others

• A passion for helping Bitwarden users

• Experience from a previous technical position (e.g. Systems Engineer, Implementation Engineer, DevOps Engineer, IT Infrastructure Engineer, etc). Equivalent education or demonstrable skills may be accepted

• Ability and desire to work remotely

Familiarity with several of the following areas/technologies is preferred:

• Bitwarden

• Linux, Windows, and macOS

• GCP, AWS, and Azure

• Android and iOS

• GitHub

• NGINX

• SQL

• TCP/IP

• DNS

• HTTP

• SMTP

• SSO implementation and best practices (SAML and OpenID Connect)

• Integrating SCIM solutions

• TLS/SSL and PKI

• RESTful APIs

WHAT TO EXPECT IN THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

• Meeting with our Recruiting Manager

• Interview with Manager of Implementation Engineering

• Interview with Implementation Engineering team members

A FEW REASONS TO WORK WITH US

• Our user community loves us and we love them. Come to work each day with a sense of purpose as we bring a more secure internet experience to everyone from our friends and family to the world’s largest organizations.

• Learn and grow. Take on new challenges with the support of your team, and join our #growth-club to continue personal and professional development.

• Administering incentive plan logic in our ICM platform , including quotas, rates, accelerators, SPIFFs, and overlay rules, and supporting rep data feeds from Salesforce and Workday, in order to keep the system aligned to approved plan documents.

• Owning the compensation inquiry and dispute queue by tracing data from booking to payout and applying structured exception handling, so that sellers receive a documented root-cause answer within SLA.

• Making the function repeatable through SOPs, data maps and dictionaries, audit-ready documentation, and automation of manual workarounds, so that sales comp scales with the go-to-market organization.

You Have

• 6+ years in an analytical role, with at least 4 years in a dedicated sales compensation function at a B2B SaaS or high-growth technology company.

• Demonstrated ownership of monthly commission close payroll handoff, accrual submission, and variance reconciliation plus hands-on administration of an enterprise ICM platform (Xactly, CaptivateIQ, Varicent, or Spiff)

• Experience managing a compensation inquiry and dispute queue with defined SLAs and structured exception handling.

• Advanced Excel and equivalent Google Sheets proficiency: multi-sheet financial models, named ranges, array formulas, XLOOKUP and INDEX-MATCH, pivot tables, and dynamic charts, built without hardcoded cell references.

• Working experience with Salesforce, including opportunity objects, field mappings, report builder, and the data pipeline that feeds commission calculations.

• A bachelor's degree or equivalent related working experience is required.

• This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

You Are

• Rigorous about accuracy: treats each payout cycle as a zero-defect process and self-audits before submission so errors don't reach sellers.

• Able to manage several concurrent workstreams against fixed close-calendar deadlines without trading off quality.

• Able to explain complex plan mechanics to a seller in plain English and present attainment analytics to a VP in a single well-structured slide.

• Comfortable diagnosing ambiguous crediting scenarios from first principles and documenting a defensible conclusion.

• Inclined to ask how a process can be made repeatable and scalable, including by applying AI and automation tools to routine comp work, rather than accepting manual workarounds.

• Familiar with SaaS revenue metrics (ARR, ACV, TCV, bookings versus revenue recognition), quota coverage ratios, and commission accrual mechanics under ASC 340-40 and 606, or willing to learn them.

Measures of success are

• Within your first month, you will have working knowledge of Collibra's core incentive comp plans and mechanics, have shadowed one to two commission closes, and be managing inquiry tickets with Senior Manager oversight on non-standard cases.

• Within your sixth month, you will hold SLA compliance above 95% on all inquiries, have zero payroll correction cycles attributable to calculation errors, and have documented SOPs for the team's top ten processes.

About Mixpanel

Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com .

About the Customer Digital Experience Team

Customer Digital Experience sits within the technical arm of Mixpanel's Customer Success organization.

Our sharpest focus is the digital-only segment: thousands of companies with no proactive account coverage. Some have technical resources available to them, but that support is entirely reactive. It answers the ticket and solves the problem in front of it. Nobody is watching for the customer who implemented and then never built a report, or the account whose usage has been sliding for a month. Our job is to be proactive,, and everything we build should be as automated as possible, without a human initiating it.

Our programs run across the full customer base and are not one-size-fits-all. We build flows that branch and adapt by segment, tuning the content, timing, and channel for who's receiving them. An onboarding flow for a digital-only customer carries the whole experience; the version reaching an account with a dedicated team is tuned to complement what that team is already doing. Same underlying program, deliberately different execution, continuously optimized based on what each segment responds to.

We're close to the data and to the technical reality of how customers implement and use Mixpanel. We're not guessing at what customers are doing; we can see it, and we build against it. This is a small, new team standing up a new function. The playbook isn't written yet; we're writing it together.

About the Role

As our Digital Adoption & Lifecycle Manager, you'll own the communications that drive adoption, retention, and expansion across Mixpanel's customer base, with our digital-only customers as the sharpest test of whether the programs work. You'll design lifecycle programs triggered by real behavior: a team that just implemented but hasn't built their first report, an account whose query volume dropped for three straight weeks, a power user hitting the edge of their current plan. Then you'll write the emails and in-product messages that move them forward.

This is a builder's role, not a maintainer's role. You'll define the segmentation, write the copy, set up the triggers, instrument the measurement, and then argue with the data about what to change.

It's also a deeply collaborative one. You'll work hand in hand with our Customer Success Digital Programs Manager, sharing a roadmap and dividing the work. You'll partner with Marketing on the overall email calendar so our lifecycle sends and their campaigns aren't competing for the same inbox. You'll support adoption initiatives coming out of Product, turning a launch into something customers actually try. And you'll take cues from customer-facing teams about what's landing and what isn't. Very little of this job happens alone.

You'll also help define what agentic customer success looks like at Mixpanel. The scaled programs we build today are rules and triggers; the ones we build next will involve AI agents that can interpret a customer's situation, decide what that customer needs, and act. We're early here and we don't have the answers. We want someone who is already experimenting, who already has opinions about where agents help and where they break trust, and who wants to shape how this gets built.

If you like clean handoffs and finished systems, this isn't it. If you want to build the thing from zero and own the number it moves, read on.

This role turns that data into multimodal AI products that change how oncologists treat patients.

We are looking for a scientific leader with a compelling vision for how foundation models can advance oncology diagnostics. You will shape our foundation model strategy - identifying the highest-value opportunities in longitudinal molecular, imaging, and clinical data, defining the capabilities we need to build, and guiding their translation into clinically useful products. This requires both the imagination to pursue new possibilities and the judgment to establish where these approaches deliver meaningful advantages. You will lead an established algorithm team, develop its technical and leadership capabilities, and recruit talent aligned with the product roadmap. With Product and other partners, you will set strategy and decide which opportunities move toward clinical deployment.

Key Responsibilities:

Build and lead the team: Grow the existing algorithm research team, hire key talent, and set a high bar for scientific rigor and execution.

Own the path from research to launch: Establish development milestones and evidence-based go/no-go criteria from feasibility through validation and launch, with clear ownership, reproducible analyses, and documented decisions.

Set strategy with Product: Partner with Product, Clinical, and Commercial leaders to prioritize clinical use cases, define intended use and success criteria, and make investment, continuation, and stop decisions based on evidence, feasibility, and clinical and business value.

Push the technical frontier: Bring in foundation models and multimodal deep learning, and turn our data into products that set us apart from competitors.

Deliver with quality: Make sure every algorithm is built on clean data, validated rigorously, and monitored after launch, so it holds up for clinicians, patients, and regulators.

Qualifications:

• Ph.D. in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Machine Learning, Biostatistics, or a related quantitative field. A Master’s degree with substantial additional experience will be considered.

• Substantial experience developing computational products, including sustained leadership of multidisciplinary teams and ownership of complex development programs through clinical deployment. Demonstrated scope and impact equivalent to a Senior Director are more important than prior title.

• Demonstrated ability to define and advance a foundation model research strategy, grounded in a deep understanding of representation learning, pretraining, adaptation, and evaluation. Able to articulate an original, clinically grounded vision, translate it into a research roadmap, and guide teams through consequential scientific and technical decisions.

• Demonstrated accountability for taking at least one AI/ML or computational algorithm from research through validation and clinical deployment within a diagnostic product. Candidates should be able to explain their decisions, validation responsibilities, cross-functional role, and post-launch results.

Able to challenge model design, data assumptions, evaluation methods, and Python-based analyses through technical reviews; routine coding is not a core responsibility.

• Demonstrated experience managing people managers and developing technical leaders, building development processes that teams adopt, and influencing senior stakeholders across R&D, Quality, Regulatory, Clinical, and Commercial without direct authority.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: United States - Remote, EMEA - Remote

Please note that we are unable to consider applications from candidates based in France, Italy, or Germany for this role.

Money is moving onto the internet, and the shift has a name: Open Money. This is money that is open, portable, agentic, and owned by you. MetaMask spent the last ten years building it; with 100M+ downloads, users in ~190 countries, and trillions in cumulative transaction volume, it's the most trusted self-custodial financial platform on the internet. Now we're building the operating system for your money: one place to hold, move, grow, and use anything you own. Join a remote-first, global team rebuilding how money works: a problem that touches everyone, every day.

About this role

We’re looking for a Senior Design Engineer to join the Consensys Design team, supporting MetaMask - the most used wallet in crypto. This is a rare opportunity to bring beautiful, intuitive experiences to millions of users engaging with decentralized applications and Web3 technologies every day.

As a Senior Design Engineer, you'll turn complex flows into simple and delightful experiences across our app and browser extension. Working closely with designers, engineers, and product managers, you'll take ideas from prototype to production - sweating the animations, haptics, and micro-interactions that make every interaction feel considered, not just functional. You'll build in React and React Native with an eye for pixel-perfect execution, contribute to our design system, and build agentic workflows that help the team move faster without cutting corners. If you love making complex things feel simple, care about craft down to the smallest detail, and want that craft in the hands of 30M+ users, this role is for you.

What You'll Do

In one sentence: Make MetaMask interactions feel intuitive, fast, and delightful - across mobile and extension

• Build pixel-perfect interfaces in React and React Native, with obsessive attention to detail.

• Design and implement animations and micro-interactions that make every tap feel considered.

• Translate Figma designs into accessible, production-ready experiences with minimal handoff friction.

• Build agentic workflows and tooling that speed up design-to-code and day-to-day engineering work.

• Grow the MetaMask design system: reusable, accessible components built to scale across platforms.

• Move from idea to prototype fast and validate with real users.

• Push for craft everywhere - the small animation nobody asked for that makes an interaction click.

Key Experience

• Portfolio demonstrating delightful, polished interfaces and interactions - not just static screens, but the motion and detail that make them feel alive.

• Proven track record shipping high-traffic, consumer-facing products in React and React Native.

• Fluency in modern JS/TypeScript and cross-platform frontend architecture: performance, accessibility, and scalable UI patterns

• An eye for interaction design and motion - you know when animations and haptics earn their place and when they're just noise.

• Strong Figma literacy - you read a design file like code.

• Good judgment about when to polish and when to ship.

• Comfortable working autonomously across a distributed, global team

• Hands-on experience with crypto wallets, blockchain, or related Web3 products.

Don't meet all the requirements? Don't sweat it. We’re passionate about building a diverse team of humans and as such, if you think you've got what it takes for our chaotic-but-fun, remote-friendly, start-up environment—apply anyway, detailing your relevant transferable skills in your cover letter. While we have a pretty good idea of what we need, we're ready for you to challenge our thinking on who needs to be in this role .

Joining Collibra's AI Sales team

Collibra's AI Sales team is at the forefront of how enterprises adopt and scale AI, selling a suite of AI products including AI Command Center, Collibra Units, and Deasy Labs, Collibra's unstructured data platform for AI, directly to the builders and technical leaders driving production AI systems. Deasy Labs, part of Collibra, develops technology that automatically discovers, enriches, and maintains the semantic context inside unstructured data. Enterprise knowledge often lives in documents, PDFs, reports, and transcripts that traditional data systems cannot easily organize or govern. The Deasy platform analyzes that content and generates structured metadata, taxonomies, and relationships that allow AI systems to retrieve the right information with accuracy and control.

You have

• Integrity - Simply put, do what you say and say what you'll do. You’re honest and forthright, have a strong moral compass, and strive to match your words with your actions while leading by example.

• Simplicity - Be like Einstein: “Everything should be made as simple as possible, but no simpler.”

• A minimum of 2 years experience in an Account Exec

Job Title: Marketing and Communications Specialist

Schedule: Approximately 20 hours per week during business hours, Monday–Friday. The selected candidate will establish a consistent weekly schedule in coordination with their supervisor and must be available for required meetings and collaborative activities.

Applicant Note: Please do not apply for this position if you are unavailable to attend onboarding on your date of hire. Onboarding is required on day one — four hours starting at 9:00 AM (2 hours organizational onboarding + 2 hours systems and tools onboarding) — and will most likely fall during your full-time job's business hours. Onboarding hours are paid. If you are unable to take off during business hours, this is not the job for you.

Compensation: $32/hr

About Virtual Peace of Mind (VPM)

Virtual Peace of Mind (VPM) is a fast-growing, fully remote mental health practice dedicated to providing evidence-based mental health services to children, adults, and families across multiple states. Our mission is to expand equitable access to mental health services through high-quality virtual care — and to support the clinicians and professionals who make that care possible.

We're building a culture that is mission-driven, accountable, supportive, and built for sustainable remote work.

Why Join VPM

At VPM, you'll be part of a team transforming access to mental health care through virtual care — with a remote model designed to support excellent work and real life.

What you can expect:

• Mission-Driven Impact: Contribute to meaningful work improving access and outcomes for youth and families.

• Remote by Design: Fully remote environment with clear expectations and supportive infrastructure.

• Collaborative Culture: Work with a multidisciplinary team that values integrity, empathy, and shared learning.

• Growth & Leadership Pathways: Opportunities to expand scope and take on leadership or consulting responsibilities as we scale.

• Professional Development: Access to training, resources, and continued learning opportunities aligned to role scope.

• State & School-Based Partnerships: Join initiatives that strengthen school-based mental health delivery and expand access across communities.

Role Overview

VPM is seeking a Marketing and Communications Specialist to tell VPM's story and keep our message consistent everywhere families, schools, and partners see us. This role owns our social media presence, creates and updates marketing materials, supports community outreach events, keeps our website and communications current, and builds the marketing funnels and automated follow-ups that turn interest from families and schools into next steps.

This is a part-time, remote role based in Virginia, with occasional travel to community events. The Marketing and Communications Specialist works closely with the CEO and the Director of Community Engagement and Partnership to make sure everything VPM puts out — from a flyer at a school event to a post on social media — reflects who we are and the care we provide. This is an organization-wide role supporting VPM's private practice, school-based programs, and other approved initiatives.

Ideal Candidate Profile

We are seeking someone who:

• Writes clearly and well — they can turn an idea into a post, a flyer, or an email without a lot of back-and-forth.

• Is organized and can manage multiple projects and deadlines at once.

• Is self-directed — they see what needs doing and do it, without waiting to be told.

• Values consistency — they care that the logo, the colors, and the message look right every time.

• Understands the mission — they care about access to mental health care and want their work to mean something.

• Is comfortable with feedback and revisions — they don't take edits personally.

• Comfortable with technology and marketing automation — they like building systems that follow up while they focus on the creative work.

• Is looking for a home, not another stop — they want to settle in and grow with the practice.

Who This Role Is Not For

This role may not be the right fit for someone who:

• Needs constant direction to get started on a task.

• Struggles to meet deadlines or juggle more than one project at a time.

• Is uncomfortable writing — most of this role is words.

• Wants a purely creative role with no coordination, admin, or follow-through.

• Is looking for a full-time position.

• Uncomfortable with technology or learning new platforms.

• Is not comfortable working independently in a remote setting.

Headquarters: Remote, Germany

Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

The Team:

Celonis grew up with the private sector: Deutsche Telekom, Mercedes-Benz, Uniper and three quarters of the DAX companies rely on Celonis Process Intelligence. Now we are taking the next big step in Germany: scaling our business with the public sector. To make this happen, Celonis is investing heavily through 2029 in its German public sector business.

Over the past year, we have built our Public Sector team from the ground up. Today, a strong go-to-market core team of Account Executives and Value Engineers is in place, working with federal and state-level institutions.

The police are one of our primary target organizations in the public sector. Police officers spend a large proportion of their time on data work and comparatively little on the actual investigation. We want to turn that around. With our new police solution, Metropolis, we help police authorities connect and make sense of their data, so that officers can focus on what matters most: solving cases and keeping people safe .

To address this, we are now complementing our existing Public Sector team with a highly specialized Account Executive who brings first-hand experience from inside the organization we serve: the Police .

The Role:

This is not a typical Account Executive role. You bring the perspective of someone who knows police work from the inside: how investigations really run, where time is lost in data work, and how decisions are made and budgets are approved. You will use this credibility to build trusted relationships with police authorities at federal and state level and position Celonis as a long-term partner for their digital transformation.

Working closely with our Public Sector AEs, Value Engineers and product experts, you will translate the operational reality of police work into compelling use cases, contribute to the creation of solution blueprints, drive opportunities from first conversation to signed contract, and help shape how Celonis enters and grows in this market.

The Work you'll do:

• Build and own relationships with police authorities at federal and state level, e.g. Bundespolizei, Bundeskriminalamt (BKA), Landeskriminalämter (LKA), Landespolizeien and the responsible Interior Ministries .

• Engage with decision-makers from police leadership, investigation units, IT and digitalization departments, and procurement

• Translate investigators' daily challenges into concrete, AI-enabled use cases for Celonis and Metropolis, with measurable impact (e.g. time saved per case, faster case processing).

• Bring the voice of the police into Celonis: share insights with our product, marketing and value engineering teams to sharpen our offering.

About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the Role:

Gusto’s looking to bring on several Staff Product Designers across our Money and HR Experience product organizations. These teams sit on some of the highest-stakes, most AI-native surfaces at Gusto, where small businesses make financial and people decisions that carry real impact, and where getting the experience right is what builds durable trust. That's exactly why judgment, taste, and craft matter here.

As a Staff Product Designer, you'll own experiences end to end within a specific domain, turning ambiguity into clear, trustworthy products and helping define patterns that don't yet exist at Gusto. You'll be deeply embedded in the product quartet, driving design decisions in partnership with Product Managers and Engineers, and demonstrating high craft and storytelling every step of the way.

This is one job posting for five open roles in Gusto Money, Banking, and HR Experiences product orgs. You'll be matched to the opportunity that best fits your strengths and interests. Here are the teams currently hiring:

• Consumer Banking: Consumer Banking builds financial products for the millions of employees paid through Gusto, anchored to Gusto Wallet — spend accounts, savings goals, paycheck splitting, and on-demand access to earned wages. Because Gusto runs payroll, the team sits at the source of income itself, helping workers smooth cash flow between paychecks, save automatically, and avoid predatory alternatives like payday lenders and overdraft fees. One of the fastest-growing engines in Gusto Banking, it moves at a startup pace while incubating 0→1 foundational technology in a regulated space where trust, reliability, and craft are everything.

•
Gusto Money: MoneyOS is the team within Gusto Money focused on helping small businesses better understand, manage, and improve their financial position. This is an especially exciting moment for the team. The space is still taking shape, which means there’s real room to define the product, the patterns, and the customer expectations. MoneyOS works at the intersection of product strategy, financial systems, customer trust, and emerging AI-native ways of building—making it a strong fit for a designer who wants to have outsized influence on both what we build and how we build it.

• HR Experiences (HRX): HRX helps small businesses get expert HR help right inside the product — a customer simply says what they need, and Gusto takes the action, answers the question, or brings in a human expert when the stakes are high. You'll design AI-native experiences across a two-sided service — the everyday self-serve moments, the AI that guides and does the work, and the human HR experts who step in when it matters most — so it all feels like one Gusto, in a domain where judgment and trust matter enormously.

Here's what you'll do day-to-day:

• Own design end to end in your domain — from framing ambiguous problems to shipping high-craft, accessible experiences that hide the underlying complexity from customers.

• Shape goals, priorities, and roadmap in partnership with your PM and engineering lead, balancing customer trust, business value, and technical realities.

Headquarters: Remote-US-CA

ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You’ll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won’t just contribute. You’ll make things happen fast.

We are looking for a Principal Software Engineer to serve as a senior technical force multiplier across three pillars of our Platform Engineering organization: Integrations, Workflows & Orchestration, and Data Management. Together, these teams own the connectors, orchestration, and data quality capabilities that push ZoomInfo's data product into the systems our customers run every day.

This is a hands-on, high-impact individual contributor role. You will embed with whichever team needs the most help at a given time. That might mean a major initiative, a stubborn area of tech debt, a reliability problem, or a chance to grow into new territory. You will lead through influence, not authority. You will set technical direction, raise the engineering bar, and work with Managers, engineers, and Product to turn ambiguity into well-architected, shipped solutions.

You will report directly to the Senior Director of Software Engineering and work closely with three Engineering Leaders and their teams.

The Three Pillars You'll Support

• Integrations: Native connectors and APIs that link ZoomInfo to CRM, marketing automation, sales engagement, data warehouse, and BI platforms (Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Outreach, Snowflake, and others), processing millions of records daily.

• Workflows & Orchestration: The engine behind lead-to-account matching and multi-step, event-driven business processes triggered by buying signals and business rules.

• Data Management: Deduplication, standardization, enrichment, continuous verification, and GDPR/CCPA compliance that keep customer data clean, current, and trustworthy.

What You'll do:

• Embed with Integrations, Workflows & Orchestration, and Data Management teams on a rotating basis, writing production-quality code and unblocking the hardest technical problems

• Define and evolve scalable, fault-tolerant, event-driven architecture on Java/Spring Boot, Node.js/NestJS, Kafka, and workflow orchestration platforms such as Temporal or Google Cloud Workflows

• Lead response and root-cause analysis for high-severity incidents and systemic reliability issues

• Drive platform modernization by consolidating integration patterns, re-architecting legacy systems, and improving observability

• Establish best practices for idempotency, retries, error handling, state management, API and webhook versioning, and workflow design

• Shape multi-quarter roadmaps with the Senior Director, Engineering Managers, and Product, bringing technical feasibility, sizing, and risk into prioritization

• Lead build-vs-buy evaluations and author architecture decision records and design docs that guide teams over multiple quarters

• Mentor engineers at all levels and serve as a senior interviewer to raise the hiring bar

What you bring:

Must-Have

• 12+ years of software engineering experience, including significant time in senior or staff-level roles, with a track record of technical leadership across multiple teams

• Deep experience designing and operating backend distributed systems at scale, with strong proficiency in Java (Spring Boot) and/or Node.js (NestJS)

• Experience building or owning integrations or connectors with CRM, marketing automation, sales engagement, or data warehouse platforms (Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Snowflake, or similar)

• Demonstrated ability to influence without authority by aligning teams, driving decisions, and earning trust across engineering, product, and business stakeholders

• Strong track record leading platform modernization, reliability, and observability initiatives, with excellent written and verbal communication skills, including presenting to executive leadership

Preferred

• Hands-on experience with event-driven architectures and streaming technologies such as Kafka, and workflow orchestration platforms such as Temporal, Google Cloud Workflows, or Airflow

• Working knowledge of data quality practices: deduplication, standardization, enrichment, and GDPR/CCPA compliance

• Experience with API strategy, webhooks, partner/ISV integration programs, and no-code/low-code workflow builders

• Experience with multi-cloud environments (AWS, GCP), build-vs-buy evaluations, vendor management, and SaaS cost optimization

Wrike is the most powerful work management platform. Built for teams and organizations looking to collaborate, create, and exceed every day, Wrike brings everyone and all work into a single place to remove complexity, increase productivity, and free people up to focus on their most purposeful work.

Wrike is our people, not a place. As a distributed team, we own our growth, stay globally connected, and rely on the product we build to deliver impactful work alongside brilliant minds. You'll have real ownership over meaningful work, a global team that has your back, and the flexibility to do your best work your way. If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

Millions of Americans feel politically homeless and left out of the two-party structure. jobs.sourceName: RSS: We Work Remotely: Sales and Marketing
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Montreal, Quebec, Canada

URL: https://www.sweatpantsagency.com/

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

•
Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.

•
Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.

•
Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.

•
Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.

•
Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.

•
Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.

•
Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.

•
Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.

•
Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.

Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

Cadence has been recognized by TIME as one of the Top 100 HealthTech Companies and by LinkedIn as a Top Startup (#4, 2025).

The Role

We’re hiring a Clinical Navigator (Medical Assistant) to deliver virtual chronic care support for Medicare patients enrolled in Cadence care programs.

Clinical Navigators deliver proactive, patient-centered outreach and follow-through. Depending on program needs, this role includes structured patient check-ins, coaching and goal-setting, care coordination to close gaps in care, and addressing barriers such as access to resources, transportation, or medication refills. Clinical Navigators document patient interactions in the Cadence platform and collaborate closely with the clinical team to escalate concerns and coordinate next steps, ensuring patients feel supported, informed, and engaged throughout their care journey.

Schedule

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States. Standard working hours are Monday through Friday, from 8am to 5pm or 9am to 6pm in your local time zone.

What You’ll Do

• Conduct outbound telephonic patient outreach and provide one-on-one coaching and support to patients managing chronic conditions, including but not limited to type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease.

• Help patients execute personalized care plans and achieve their goals by providing education and coaching focused on behavior modification, nutrition, physical activity, and self-management strategies using evidence-based techniques such as motivational interviewing and SMART goals.

• Conduct comprehensive assessments of patients' health status, lifestyle behaviors, nutritional habits, and readiness to change.

• Educate patients on disease management, medication adherence, symptom recognition, and prevention strategies, and execute care delivery tasks in accordance with Cadence clinical policies and established protocols, under appropriate clinical supervision.

• Monitor patients' progress, adherence to treatment plans, and health outcomes through regular check-ins and remote monitoring tools.

• Document patient interactions, outcomes, and follow-up plans in the Cadence platform; identify barriers to care (including social needs) and connect patients with resources or internal support pathways.

• Collaborate in real time with clinicians and patient support teams using tools such as our Cadence Platform, Google Workspace, and Slack, and contribute feedback to improve workflows in a fast-moving, change-oriented environment.

These responsibilities are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by personnel assigned to this job classification. They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of job duties performed by personnel in this classification. Other job related duties may be assigned by management.

Who You Are

• A clinician who thrives at the intersection of rigorous care standards and a care delivery model that is still being built.

• Skilled in patient education, coaching, and care coordination - you meet patients where they are in life, considering their age, lifestyle, and diet.

• Disciplined in documentation and follow-through, with the attention to detail required for accurate clinical records in a remote environment.

Cadence is the clinical AI company automating the treatment of chronic disease. Its Clinical Intelligence takes on the routine, high-volume work of chronic care – monitoring patients, surfacing risks, and coordinating action – so clinicians can focus on the decisions that require them. Grounded in partnerships with more than 20 leading health systems, deep EMR integrations, dedicated medical group, and experience serving a population of more than 100,000 patients, the system learns from real-world care delivery, improving as it scales. Cadence has been recognized by TIME as one of the Top 100 HealthTech Companies and by LinkedIn as a Top Startup (#4, 2025).

The Role

We’re hiring a Clinical Navigator (Licensed Practical Nurse) to deliver virtual chronic care support for Medicare patients enrolled in Cadence care programs.

Clinical Navigators deliver proactive, patient-centered outreach and follow-through. Depending on program needs, this role includes structured patient check-ins, coaching and goal-setting, care coordination to close gaps in care, and addressing barriers such as access to resources, transportation, or medication refills. Clinical Navigators document patient interactions in the Cadence platform and collaborate closely with the clinical team to escalate concerns and coordinate next steps, ensuring patients feel supported, informed, and engaged throughout their care journey.

Schedule

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States. Standard working hours are Monday through Friday, from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM or 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM in the Pacific time zone.

What You’ll Do

• Conduct outbound telephonic patient outreach and provide one-on-one coaching and support to patients managing chronic conditions, including but not limited to type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease.

• Help patients execute personalized care plans and achieve their goals by providing education and coaching focused on behavior modification, nutrition, physical activity, and self-management strategies using evidence-based techniques such as motivational interviewing and SMART goals.

• Conduct comprehensive assessments of patients' health status, lifestyle behaviors, nutritional habits, and readiness to change.

• Educate patients on disease management, medication adherence, symptom recognition, and prevention strategies, and execute care delivery tasks in accordance with Cadence clinical policies and established protocols, under appropriate clinical supervision.

• Monitor patients' progress, adherence to treatment plans, and health outcomes through regular check-ins and remote monitoring tools.

• Document patient interactions, outcomes, and follow-up plans in the Cadence platform; identify barriers to care (including social needs) and connect patients with resources or internal support pathways.

• Collaborate in real time with clinicians and patient support teams using tools such as our Cadence Platform, Google Workspace, and Slack, and contribute feedback to improve workflows in a fast-moving, change-oriented environment.

These responsibilities are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by personnel assigned to this job classification. They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of job duties performed by personnel in this classification. Other job related duties may be assigned by management.

Who You Are

• A clinician who thrives at the intersection of rigorous care standards and a care delivery model that is still being built.

• Skilled in patient education, coaching, and care coordination - you meet patients where they are in life, considering their age, lifestyle, and diet.

• Disciplined in documentation and follow-through, with the attention to detail required for accurate clinical records in a remote environment.

• Reliable and consistent in schedule adherence, with the interpersonal communication skills to build trust with patients over the phone.

• Comfortable working independently in a remote, fast-paced environment with evolving workflows, and tech-savvy enough to navigate and troubleshoot multiple systems simultaneously while keeping patients engaged.

• Comfortable using AI-assisted clinical tools (such as Gemini or Open Evidence) to support patient interactions and surface relevant clinical context, while maintaining clinical judgment as the primary guide for every patient decision.

ABOUT THE COMPANY:
The company is a Melbourne-based landscape design studio founded by Drew Burns, specialising in native and climate-adaptive gardens for residential clients across Melbourne and the Mornington Peninsula. The client's philosophy is simple: every project starts with a clear plan that resolves layout, levels, materials, and planting before anything is built - so construction happens without guesswork, miscommunication, or costly rework.
The studio's process runs in two stages: a concept report developed locally with the client, followed by detailed construction drawings. We're growing our team to bring the construction drawing stage in-house on an offshore basis, freeing up our local design team to focus on new client work while drawings progress in the background.

ROLE OVERVIEW:
We're looking for a skilled CAD draftsperson to take finalised landscape design concepts and turn them into accurate, buildable construction drawing sets. This is a genuine long-term team role, not a one-off gig - we're investing in someone who wants to grow with the business, not just complete tasks.
The ideal candidate is confident in producing both construction drawings and photorealistic renders, giving us a single point of contact who can carry a project from concept through to construction-ready documentation.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Convert approved concept designs into detailed, accurate construction drawing sets (setout plans, levels, sections, details, planting plans, and material schedules).

• Work primarily in Vectorworks to ensure drawings are consistent with the client's existing file standards and templates.

• Produce photorealistic or presentation-quality renders to support client approvals, where required.

• Liaise with Drew and the local design team to clarify design intent, resolve details, and incorporate feedback.

• Maintain drawing accuracy for levels, drainage falls, and material junctions so drawings are genuinely buildable on site.

• Manage your own workflow and deadlines across multiple concurrent projects, flagging risks or delays early.

• Keep drawing files, layers, and naming conventions organised and consistent across projects.

• Proven, verifiable proficiency in Vectorworks is strongly preferred.

• Candidates with strong experience in SketchUp, Revit, or AutoCAD will also be considered - we're open to supporting a transition to Vectorworks.

• Background in landscape architecture, landscape design, or architectural drafting, ideally with residential project experience.

• Understanding of construction documentation: setout, levels, sections, details, and materials - not just drafting for visual presentation.

• Rendering skills (e.g, Enscape, D5) are a strong advantage.

• Strong written English for clear communication with the Australian-based team.

• Reliable internet connection and the ability to work overlapping hours with an Australian (Melbourne, AEST/AEDT) team.

What We're Looking For
Technical skill matters, but it's not the only thing we're hiring for. We value:

• Genuine attention to detail - drawings that are accurate the first time, not just "close enough."

• Strong work ethic and reliability - someone who owns their workload and communicates proactively.

• A long-term mindset - we're looking to invest in this role and grow it over time, not treat it as disposable outsourced labour.

• Honesty about your actual skill level and software experience - we'd rather know upfront than discover gaps later.

It brings together the context that usually lives across CRM, docs, dashboards, tools, and people’s heads: who we sell to, why customers buy, what matters now, what we tried, and what worked. Agents and people use that context to decide what to do next and execute across the GTM stack.

You’ll write a lot of the early code yourself, make the key technical decisions, and shape the product as we learn what works.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: US - Remote

Our team is committed to enhancing physician and patient quality of life through Elation, a SaaS cloud-based clinical platform. Since inception, we've been focused on building a world-class technology solution that creates an experience of delight and ease for physicians, and that our users love.

Every signed customer agreement at Elation passes through a final review before billing and onboarding begin. That review confirms what the customer signed matches what we set up in Salesforce: the right products, quantities, prices, and dates. When it's done well, customers get billed correctly from day one and our finance and customer success teams avoid costly cleanup later.We are looking for a Contract Operations Associate to join our Business Systems Team on a contract basis and own a share of these reviews. You'll work from clear checklists and procedures, use AI-assisted review tools, and partner closely with the specialists who own this process. This is a great fit for someone early in their career who is detail oriented, enjoys getting things exactly right, and wants hands-on exposure to how a SaaS company runs its revenue operations.

What You'll Do

Contract Review & Verification

• Own a daily review queue of signed deals awaiting final approval, starting with new customer agreements, downgrades, and simple add-ons (adding a product or seats), then expanding to renewals and other deal types as you ramp.

• Confirm the signed order form is complete : both the customer and Elation have signed and dated it, and you identify the official execution date.

• Check that key dates line up across the order form, the Salesforce opportunity, and the quote (execution date, close date, and contract start date), and that add-ons end on the same date as the customer's existing contract.

• Reconcile the quote against the order form line by line: products, quantities, terms, unit prices, and totals, including confirming that unchanged products and removed products are recorded correctly.

• Verify approvals and required data : discounts have a documented approval, required fields are filled in, and the customer account is a real, active practice rather than a trial.

• Correct routine issues directly in Salesforce (e.g., date fields or account details) when the procedure allows it, then advance the deal to Closed Won.

• Confirm downstream handoffs fired after approval, such as the customer's billing record and onboarding project being created, and flag anything that didn't.

Partnering with Sales & Customer Success on Corrections

• Return deals that need fixing to the account executive or customer success manager who owns them, with a clear, specific note: what doesn't match, where you found it (order form page, quote line, field), and what correct looks like.

• Follow corrections through to completion : track returned deals, check that the fix is right when they come back, and re-review promptly so customers aren't left waiting on billing or onboarding.

• Prioritize with deal owners during busy periods like month end, communicating which deals are blocked and what's needed to close them on time.

• Spot repeat issues by rep, team, or deal type and share them with the team, so we can improve training, Salesforce guardrails, and error messages and prevent the same mistake next time.

Resolving Open Questions with Stakeholders

• Bring questions to the right person with full context : the deal link, what you checked, what's unclear, and your best guess at the answer. Start with the team's operations specialist, then partner with Deal Desk, Customer Success leadership, Finance (billing and revenue reporting), or Salesforce administrators as directed.

• Escalate anything outside the checklist rather than making judgment calls on your own, such as contract exceptions, non-standard discounts, unusual date requests, or large and custom agreements.

• Track every open question until it's resolved , keeping the deal owner updated so nothing stalls silently in the queue.

• Capture the answer once a question is settled, adding it to the procedure or FAQ so the next reviewer doesn't have to ask again.

Tools, Documentation & Continuous Improvement

• Run AI-assisted review tools first on each deal, then complete the manual checklist and confirm or correct the tool's results; your corrections help improve the automation.

• Log issues and root causes in our ticketing system for any deal that didn't pass cleanly.

• Flag gaps or confusing steps in our procedures; your feedback directly shapes the documentation and training for future reviewers.

What You Bring

• Attention to detail : you notice when two documents don't match, and you double-check before calling something done.

• Process discipline : comfortable following a checklist exactly, every time, and keeping clean records of your work.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: Canada - Remote

Elation Health is deeply committed to helping independent primary care practices take better care of their patients. Since 2010, we've built a clinical-first, collaborative EHR platform — and with the addition of Elation Billing, we're bringing that same clinical-first philosophy to the revenue side of the practice, so billing works with the chart instead of around it.

Elation Health is searching for a Support Subject Matter Expert in Elation Billing — someone who has already done real medical billing and revenue cycle management work, not someone learning it on the job. This is a hands-on, case-based role embedded directly in our support queue: you'll bring practitioner-level RCM judgment to the billing cases our Technical Support Specialists can't fully resolve through process or AI-assisted troubleshooting alone, and you'll help the rest of the team get sharper at spotting those cases in the first place.

This isn't a back-office consulting role. You'll be working live cases day to day alongside our support team, diagnosing whether an issue is a product bug, a payer-specific quirk, or a mismatch between how a practice actually operates and how they've configured their billing workflow — then resolving it with the kind of judgment that only comes from having sat inside a claims lifecycle before.

Responsibilities

• Serve as the Elation Billing product line's embedded RCM expert, owning complex billing and revenue cycle cases that require practitioner-level judgment — claims lifecycle issues, CPT/ICD-10 coding logic, payer adjudication and denial patterns, A/R and collections workflows.

• Act as the go-to resource for case swarms and escalations within Elation Billing whenever a Technical Support Specialist's investigation surfaces a billing nuance beyond scripted troubleshooting.

• Diagnose a practice's underlying billing context — payment model (insurance-taking vs. DPC), staffing structure, and prior workflow choices — to distinguish genuine product issues from configuration or workflow mismatches, rather than treating every case as a symptom in isolation.

• Partner with Product and Prod Dev, turning recurring billing edge cases, payer-specific patterns, and denial trends into structured feedback that can inform the roadmap.

• Contribute to and maintain the team's billing-related knowledge base, SOPs, and macros, and help calibrate the AI Case Assistant's billing-related suggestions so resolutions compound across the team rather than living only in your own case history.

• Help build the broader team's baseline RCM literacy — sharing real-world billing context so Specialists can better anticipate the issues different practice types are prone to.

• Track and report on billing-case quality and resolution metrics within your scope, and flag systemic patterns rather than resolving the same root cause case-by-case indefinitely.

Requirements

• 3+ years of hands-on medical billing / revenue cycle management experience — claims submission, payer follow-up, denial management, and A/R — brought in from outside a support organization, not built up through support tenure.

• Working fluency in CPT/ICD-10 coding logic, claims adjudication, and payer-specific billing rules across commercial and government payers.

• Experience working within an EHR, practice management, or medical billing platform (e.g., Epic, athenahealth, Waystar, or similar).

• Strong written and verbal communicator, able to translate complex billing and RCM concepts into clear guidance for both practices and internal teams.

• Comfortable working directly in a live case queue - this is a frontline, hands-on role, not a periodic-consulting one.

• Self-directed and detail-oriented, with the judgment to know when a case needs to go beyond a scripted answer.

Preferred

• Certification such as CPB (Certified Professional Biller), CRCR (Certified Revenue Cycle Representative), or CHFP (in progress or completed).

• Prior experience supporting independent primary care or small-group practices specifically.

• Experience on a support, customer success, or implementation team at a SaaS/EHR company.

• Exposure to AI-assisted support or case-management tooling.

• Six Sigma, Lean, or other process-improvement background.

Freestar's publishers need partners who can grow with them — and the Senior CSM role exists for someone who brings that depth. You own a portfolio of Freestar's more complex, higher-stakes publisher relationships, operating with a level of autonomy and strategic influence that goes beyond day-to-day account management.

You've been in this industry long enough to have developed real pattern recognition. You know what good monetization looks like across different publisher types, you can spot a floor pricing problem before it shows up in the numbers, and you've had enough difficult client conversations to navigate them without breaking a sweat. You don't need a playbook for every situation — and when one is missing, you help build it.

This role sits at the intersection of trusted advisor and yield expert. Your publishers should feel like they have a genuine advocate inside Freestar, and your peers should feel like they have a resource they can learn from.

What You'll Do

Publisher Partnership

• Own a portfolio of Freestar's more complex publisher accounts, serving as their primary strategic point of contact

• Lead executive business reviews with a clear point of view — not just a performance recap, but a forward-looking perspective on where the relationship should go

• Build deep, multi-threaded relationships within publisher organizations, spanning revenue, ad ops, product, and editorial

• Anticipate risks and opportunities before they're surfaced by the publisher, and come to every conversation prepared with a recommendation

Yield & Optimization

• Take ownership of performance analysis end-to-end — identifying trends, forming hypotheses, designing tests, and tracking outcomes across your portfolio

• Drive more sophisticated optimization work: auction dynamics, floor pricing strategy, identity and audience approaches, format diversification, and the interplay between user experience and revenue

• Serve as a technical resource for both your publishers and your peers — able to go deep on programmatic mechanics and explain them clearly to any audience

• Collaborate with yield, demand, and product teams on bespoke solutions for accounts with unique needs or meaningful scale

Strategic Growth

• Identify and develop expansion opportunities that are genuinely additive — new products, formats, or services that make sense for each publisher's specific situation

• Contribute meaningfully to renewal conversations, bringing a clear account narrative and commercial instincts to the table

• Flag patterns you're seeing across your portfolio that could inform product development, demand strategy, or CS process improvements

Team Contribution

• Mentor and support junior CSMs, sharing your experience and helping elevate the team's collective standard

• Help build and refine playbooks, QBR templates, and best practices based on what you're learning in your accounts

• Contribute to onboarding and training as a subject matter resource

What We're Looking For

• 5–8 years of experience in customer success, account management, or a publisher-facing role within ad tech or programmatic advertising

• Proven track record managing complex, high-value accounts with multiple stakeholders

• Deep, working knowledge of the programmatic ecosystem — header bidding, floor pricing, auction mechanics, yield optimization, GAM, and identity solutions

• Strong analytical instincts: you're comfortable owning performance analysis independently and turning data into a clear narrative

• Executive presence and communication skills — able to hold a room at the VP or C-suite level without leaning on a script

• A coaching mindset — you share what you know and make the people around you better

• Self-directed and proactive; you manage a complex book without needing to be prompted

Bonus points for:

• Experience on the publisher side — you've sat in the seat your partners are sitting in

• Familiarity with identity and audience solutions (UID2, RampID, first-party data strategies)

• Experience with CMP/consent frameworks and their downstream monetization impact

• Comfort with CS and CRM platforms and using data to manage a book systematically

jobs.title: Strategy Lead (market-leading GEO / SEO agency)
jobs.sourceName: RSS: We Work Remotely: Sales and Marketing
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Oxford, UK

URL: https://getellipsis.com

Ellipsis is fast becoming the market leader in "GEO" for B2B technology companies. This is a senior, hands-on role in a fast-moving and ambitious agency.

The move to AI search has put a lot of the SEO industry on the back foot. Ellipsis has always been consultative and strategic in our approach. We started building AI search products in 2021 on GPT-2, so this has been a time for us to thrive.

We think we understand AI search better than almost anyone. We have our own tracking product, ~25 million AI answers to analyze (with more tracked every week), and execution end-to-end: strategy, writing, in-house design, optimization, and performance reporting.

Marketing teams everywhere are working out what AI search means for them, and we're one of the few firms with credible answers backed by work we've already done. That's taking us beyond B2B tech scale-ups into conversations with global retailers, banks, and consumer brands, and into work well beyond search: positioning, websites, and how buyers choose between suppliers.

As Strategy Lead, you'll decide what work we do for every client, and why, and shape how our latest research on AI Search feeds into this decision. You'll run the Strategy team, set the strategy for our biggest accounts yourself, and build a strategy service that holds its quality as we take on much larger projects.

What you'll own

You'll own strategy across Ellipsis: what we recommend for each client, in what order, and why. You’ll ensure that all work we do for clients is adapted based on our constantly growing understanding of AI Search. You'll report directly to the MD/Founder and sit on the leadership team alongside the Accounts Lead, Head of Operations, and Chief of Staff.

Ellipsis is at the forefront of demand as SEO turns into GEO. We are growing very quickly as buyers are deciding now whom to trust with AI search, and some are bringing us in at board level as part of their AI strategy. The firms that earn those relationships over the next year will be hard to replace.

Our view is that AI makes yesterday's expertise cheap, so the job is to keep producing today's expertise and applying it well. Every client project should teach us more about what works, and that learning should make the next project faster and better. You’ll work closely with our Research and Development analyst to shape overall strategy, work with the team to ensure this is effectively used in practice, and ensure we have an effective feedback loop of findings <> implementation <> upskilling the team to ask better questions <> identifying gaps and new research.

Your job is to provide strategic judgement and ensure work gets done across the whole team. We have more data, tooling and ideas than any single client needs! And so your role will be identifying the leverage points across our customers; what can be done that makes performance better across the board? How can we deliver more of what our clients need? How can we build or improve automations that help us deliver more value? How do we apply findings, data, and research that actually lands?

You will own a couple of (high level or at risk – depending where you are most needed) clients and will need to be comfortable presenting, answering hard questions from clients, and building trust with our customers. You’ll need to be doing client work in order to understand how we do Strategy, what works, etc.; but client work is a max of 50% of the role.

You will work closely with other senior members of the team: our Accounts Lead owns client relationships, and you will need to collaborate closely; our Head of Operations owns capacity and process; our Founder&MD leads the business and is hands-on in the weeds with clients; and we’re currently hiring a Research and Development analyst to own the research (currently this is split across the team). You’ll also need to work closely with our Writing team and Content team to ensure questions are answered, strategy is understood, and everyone is doing the right work!

You will lead and line manage our Strategy team (currently 3); their personal development and progression is very important and you will have the chance to shape their up-skilling and growth! Search is changing quickly, and you’ll help our ambitious team progress rapidly.

How we'll measure it

We want to see progress in the key metrics we and our clients care about across the board – clients recommended, and picked, more often on the buying questions that matter to them, and that showing up in their pipeline. Alongside it, we want to see progress in the whole Strategy team's output: more clients and larger programmes carried by the same people, without quality slipping, and progress / progression for the team members too. Our understanding of AI Search continues to develop, and you’ll be instrumental in ensuring the work we do for clients adapts quickly to our latest research.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

The Nordic team is a high-velocity, solution-oriented sales team dedicated to capturing market share and landing the region's next generation of high-growth tech companies and enterprise category leaders. From Maersk to Lovable, we win new business by showing companies how Stripe’s financial infrastructure unlocks new revenue streams and powers international expansion.

What you’ll do

As an Enterprise Account Executive covering new business, you’ll identify new opportunities to expand Stripe’s footprint. Specifically, we’re looking for someone who can execute on long-term sales strategies, engage with internal and external stakeholders, align on technical and business requirements with product teams, build value in competitive situations, lead commercial negotiations, and close deals.

You will screen for roles across our San Diego corporate team and our warehouse and fulfillment operation in Fort Worth, Texas. This is a focused role. Your job is to hold a consistent, fair bar across high volume screens so our recruiters spend their time on candidates who are truly ready.
If you take pride in sound judgment, clear notes, and doing the details right every time, we would love to meet you!
